title: Solving for x
desc: Use inverse operations to isolate x. What you do to one side of the equation, do to the other. For 2x + 3 = 11, subtract 3 from both sides, then divide both sides by 2 to get x = 4.
prompts: how do i solve for x
how do i isolate x in an equation
i need to get x by itself
how do i find x in an equation

title: Slope of a line
desc: Slope is the steepness of a line: rise over run, or the change in y divided by the change in x. A slope of 2/3 means the line goes up 2 units when it goes right 3 units. A negative slope goes down as it goes right.
prompts: what is the slope of a line
what does rise over run mean
how do i calculate slope from two points

title: Linear equations
desc: A linear equation graphs as a straight line. A common form is y = mx + b, where m is the slope and b is the y-intercept, the point where the line crosses the y-axis.
prompts: what does y = mx + b mean

title: Inequalities
desc: An inequality compares values with symbols such as <, >, ≤ or ≥. Solving one is like solving an equation, except that multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
prompts: what is an inequality in math
how do i solve an inequality
when do i flip the inequality sign
what does less than or equal to mean

title: Systems of equations
desc: A system is two or more equations considered together. A solution is a set of values that makes every equation true. You can solve by graphing, substitution, or elimination, which adds or subtracts equations to cancel a variable.
prompts: what is a system of equations
how do i solve two equations
how do systems of equations work
find x and y that work in both equations

title: The Pythagorean theorem
desc: In a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle, and a and b are the other two sides. If the legs are 3 and 4, the hypotenuse is 5.
prompts: how do i find the hypotenuse
how do i use pythagorean theorem

title: Similar triangles
desc: Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size. Their corresponding angles are equal, and corresponding sides are in the same ratio. You can use that ratio to find a missing side.
prompts: how do i find a missing side in similar triangles

title: Volume of a cylinder
desc: The volume of a cylinder is πr²h, the area of the circular base times the height. Use the same units for the radius and the height, and the result is in cubic units.
prompts: how do i find the volume of a cylinder
what is the cylinder volume formula
volume of a can or tube
area of the base times height

title: Volume of a sphere
desc: The volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³, where r is the radius, the distance from the center to any point on the surface. If you know the diameter, divide it by 2 first to get the radius.
prompts: how do i find the volume of a sphere
what is the sphere volume formula

title: Percent change
desc: Percent change is the difference divided by the original amount, then multiplied by 100. A price that goes from $40 to $50 rises by 10/40, which is a 25 percent increase. A decrease uses the same formula and comes out negative or is called a decrease.
prompts: how do i calculate percent change
how do i find percent increase
how do i find percent decrease
how much did it increase by percent

title: Proportions
desc: A proportion says two ratios are equal, such as 2/3 = 4/6. To solve for a missing value, you can cross-multiply: if a/b = c/d, then a times d equals b times c.
prompts: what is a proportion in math
how do i solve a proportion
if a over b equals c over d
finding a missing number in a proportion

title: Speed, distance and time
desc: Speed equals distance divided by time. Distance equals speed times time, and time equals distance divided by speed. Use matching units, such as miles and hours if the speed is in miles per hour.
prompts: how do i find time from speed and distance
how do i find distance from speed and time
how long will it take to travel
what is the formula for speed
convert hours and miles for speed

title: Graphing a line
desc: Pick x-values, compute the matching y-values from the equation, and plot those points. For y = mx + b, start at the y-intercept, then use the slope to find another point: rise the numerator and run the denominator.
prompts: how do i graph a line
how do i plot y equals mx plus b
use slope to find the next point
start at the y intercept then rise over run
how do i draw a straight line from an equation
plot points on a coordinate plane

title: The distributive property
desc: The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply the factor outside the parentheses by each term inside, and keep each term's sign. For example, 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12.
prompts: how do i distribute in math
how does the distributive property work

title: Combining like terms
desc: Like terms have the same variable raised to the same power, such as 3x and 5x. Add or subtract their coefficients and keep the variable part: 3x + 5x = 8x. Constants combine with constants, and 3x and 3x² are not like terms.
prompts: how do i combine like terms
what are like terms in algebra
can i add x and x squared
simplify an expression by combining terms
like terms same variable same power

title: Scientific notation
desc: Scientific notation writes a number as a value between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of 10. 5,400 is 5.4 × 10³, and 0.0032 is 3.2 × 10⁻³. A positive exponent means a larger number; a negative exponent means a fraction less than 1.
prompts: how do i write a number in scientific notation
how do powers of ten work
what does a negative exponent mean in scientific notation
convert scientific notation to a regular number

title: Independent events
desc: Two events are independent if one outcome does not change the probability of the other, such as two flips of a fair coin. For independent events, multiply their probabilities: the chance of heads then heads is 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.
prompts: what are independent events in probability
does one event affect the other
probability of two things both happening

title: The scientific method
desc: The scientific method is a way to test ideas: ask a question, form a hypothesis, plan a fair test, collect data, and draw a conclusion. Other people should be able to repeat the test to see if they get similar results.
prompts: how do scientists test an idea
how does the scientific method work
why do experiments need to be repeatable
scientific method for a school project

title: Hypotheses and theories
desc: A hypothesis is a testable possible explanation for something you observed. A scientific theory is a well-supported explanation built from many tested hypotheses and a large body of evidence, not a guess. Theories can still be revised if new evidence appears.
prompts: is a theory just a guess
how is a theory different from a hypothesis
what does theory mean in science

title: Atoms
desc: An atom is the basic unit of a chemical element. It has a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around the nucleus. The number of protons, called the atomic number, identifies the element.
prompts: what is an atom made of
what does the atomic number mean
what is in the nucleus of an atom

title: Molecules
desc: A molecule is two or more atoms bonded together. The atoms can be the same, as in O₂, or different, as in water, H₂O. The chemical formula tells you which atoms are in the molecule and how many of each.
prompts: how is a molecule different from an atom

title: The periodic table
desc: The periodic table organizes elements by atomic number. Rows are called periods and columns are called groups. Elements in the same group often have similar chemical properties, such as the noble gases in the far-right column.
prompts: how is the periodic table organized
why are elements in the same column similar
how do i read the periodic table
atomic number on the periodic table

title: States of matter
desc: The common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas. In a solid, particles are packed in a fixed shape. In a liquid they flow and take the shape of the container. In a gas they spread out to fill the available space. Heat or pressure can change the state.
prompts: what are the states of matter
how do particles move in a gas
what's the difference between a solid and a liquid
what is a gas made of
plasma is a state of matter

title: Density
desc: Density is mass divided by volume. A material with higher density has more mass in the same amount of space. That is why a steel bolt sinks in water while a larger piece of wood can float: steel’s density is greater than water’s, and most wood is less dense than water.
prompts: why does density decide if something floats
why does steel sink and wood float

title: Acids and bases
desc: Acids and bases are opposite kinds of substances in water. Acids increase hydrogen ion concentration and often taste sour, such as lemon juice. Bases decrease that concentration or increase hydroxide, and many feel slippery, such as soap. They can neutralize each other.
prompts: what is a base in chemistry
how do acids and bases work

title: pH
desc: pH is a scale that usually runs from 0 to 14 and measures how acidic or basic a water solution is. 7 is neutral, like pure water. Numbers below 7 are acidic and numbers above 7 are basic. Each step of 1 is a tenfold change in acidity.
prompts: how does the ph scale work
what does a low ph mean

title: Chemical versus physical change
desc: A physical change alters form but not the substance itself, such as melting ice or tearing paper. A chemical change makes a new substance, such as burning wood or baking a cake. Clues can include a new color, gas, temperature change or unexpected solid, though those clues are not proof by themselves.
prompts: is melting ice a chemical change
is burning wood a chemical change
how can i tell chemical from physical change
difference between chemical and physical change

title: Animal and plant cells
desc: Both animal and plant cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm and a cell membrane. Plant cells also have a cell wall and usually chloroplasts for photosynthesis, and they often have a large central vacuole. Animal cells do not have a cell wall or chloroplasts.
prompts: what's the difference between plant and animal cells
what do plant cells have that animal cells don't
do animal cells have a cell wall
nucleus in plant and animal cells

title: DNA
desc: DNA is the molecule in cells that carries genetic instructions. It is shaped like a double helix, a twisted ladder, with paired bases: A with T, and C with G. Those instructions help determine how an organism grows and how its cells work.

title: Food chains
desc: A food chain shows how energy moves from one living thing to another. It often starts with a producer, such as a plant, that makes its own food. A consumer eats plants or other animals, and a decomposer breaks down dead material. Arrows point toward the eater, the direction energy flows.
prompts: what is a producer in a food chain
what do the arrows in a food chain mean
what is a consumer in science
how does a food chain work

title: Ecosystems
desc: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the nonliving parts of their environment, such as water, soil, air and climate. A change in one part, like a drought or the loss of a species, can affect many other parts.
prompts: living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem
what happens if a species disappears
community of organisms and their environment

title: The water cycle
desc: The water cycle is the movement of water between Earth’s surface and the atmosphere. Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, and falls as precipitation. It can then flow as runoff, soak into the ground, or evaporate again.
prompts: how does the water cycle work
runoff and groundwater in the water cycle
how does water move on earth

title: The solar system
desc: The solar system is the Sun and everything that orbits it, including eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets. The four inner planets are rocky. The four outer planets are much larger and are mostly gas and ice. Gravity from the Sun keeps the planets in orbit.
prompts: why do planets stay in orbit

title: Solar and lunar eclipses
desc: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and the Moon’s shadow falls on Earth. A lunar eclipse happens when Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon and Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon. They do not occur every month because the Moon’s orbit is tilted.
prompts: difference between solar and lunar eclipse
why don't eclipses happen every month
moon between the sun and earth
when can i see an eclipse

title: Plate tectonics
desc: Earth’s outer shell is broken into large plates that move slowly over the mantle. Where plates meet they can pull apart, collide, or slide past each other. That movement helps explain earthquakes, many volcanoes, and the building of mountain ranges.

title: Earthquakes
desc: An earthquake is the shaking caused when rocks along a fault suddenly slip and release energy as seismic waves. Most earthquakes occur near tectonic plate boundaries. During shaking, drop to the ground, take cover under sturdy furniture, and hold on until it stops.
prompts: what should i do during an earthquake
what is a fault in geology

title: Volcanoes
desc: A volcano is an opening where molten rock, ash and gas can reach the surface. Most volcanoes form near plate boundaries, especially where a plate sinks or where plates pull apart. Magma is molten rock underground; once it reaches the surface it is called lava.
prompts: what is the difference between magma and lava
what comes out of a volcano

title: Fossils
desc: Fossils are remains or traces of past life, such as bones, shells, footprints or leaf impressions, preserved in rock. They form more often when an organism is buried quickly and hard parts are slowly replaced or left as an imprint. Fossils help scientists learn how life and environments have changed.
prompts: how do we learn from fossils
preserved remains of plants and animals

title: Acceleration
desc: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. An object accelerates if it speeds up, slows down, or changes direction. In everyday use people often say acceleration only for speeding up, but in physics all of those changes count.
prompts: does changing direction count as acceleration

title: Kinetic and potential energy
desc: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. Potential energy is stored energy because of position or condition, such as a bike at the top of a hill or a stretched spring. Energy can change from one form to the other, like a ball slowing as it rolls uphill and speeding up as it comes down.
prompts: energy of motion versus stored energy
bike at the top of a hill
difference between kinetic and potential energy

title: Simple circuits
desc: A simple electric circuit is a closed loop that lets current flow from a power source through a load, such as a bulb, and back again. If the loop is broken, the current stops. A switch opens or closes the loop, and wires need a complete path of conductive material.
prompts: how does a switch work in a circuit

title: Electrical conductors
desc: An electrical conductor lets electric current flow easily. Metals such as copper and aluminum are common conductors and are used in wires. An electrical insulator, such as rubber, glass or many plastics, resists current and is used to coat wires for safety.
prompts: why are wires made of copper
why is rubber around a wire

title: The greenhouse effect
desc: The greenhouse effect is the way some gases in the atmosphere, including carbon dioxide and water vapor, absorb heat and keep Earth warmer than it would be without them. A stronger greenhouse effect from extra greenhouse gases traps more heat and raises global average temperatures.
prompts: why does carbon dioxide trap heat
is the greenhouse effect always bad
what gases cause the greenhouse effect
how does the greenhouse effect warm the earth

title: Renewable energy
desc: Renewable energy comes from sources that are naturally replenished, such as sunlight, wind, moving water and geothermal heat. Fossil fuels like coal, oil and natural gas form much more slowly than we use them. Renewable sources still have costs, land use and other tradeoffs, but they do not run out in the same way.

title: Recycling
desc: Recycling turns used materials into new products instead of throwing them away. Rinse containers, follow your local rules, and keep items loose rather than bagged unless your collector says otherwise. Not everything with a recycling symbol is accepted curbside, so check the local list.
prompts: do i need to rinse containers
what does the recycling symbol mean
how do i recycle at home

title: The atmosphere
desc: Earth’s atmosphere is the layer of gases around the planet. It is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, with smaller amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and other gases. It provides air to breathe, helps protect the surface from much of the Sun’s harmful radiation, and is where weather happens.
prompts: what gases are in the atmosphere
how does the atmosphere protect us
nitrogen and oxygen in the air

title: Microscopes
desc: A microscope magnifies things that are too small to see clearly with your eyes alone. A compound light microscope uses lenses and light; start on the lowest power, use the coarse knob to find the specimen, then sharpen with the fine knob. Keep slides thin and never use the coarse knob on high power.
prompts: how do i use a microscope
how does a light microscope work
tips for using a school microscope

title: The human heart
desc: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood through the body. The right side sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen. The left side sends oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body. Valves keep blood moving in one direction.
prompts: what does the human heart do
right side versus left side of the heart
why does blood go to the lungs
how does the heart pump blood

title: The lungs
desc: The lungs are where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it. When you inhale, air travels down the windpipe to smaller airways and into tiny air sacs called alveoli. Oxygen crosses into the blood there, and carbon dioxide crosses out to be exhaled.
prompts: how does oxygen get into the blood

title: Digestion
desc: Digestion breaks food into nutrients the body can absorb. It starts in the mouth with chewing and saliva, continues in the stomach, and most nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine. The large intestine absorbs water and forms leftover material into stool.
prompts: what happens to food after you eat
what does the small intestine do
what does the stomach do in digestion
does digestion start in the mouth
what does the large intestine do
